relations.statement: For a box X and continuous F with interval Jacobian enclosure, if K(X) = c - Y F(c) + (I - Y J(X))(X - c) is disjoint from X, then F has no zero in X (contrapositive of: zero in X implies zero in K(X) ∩ X).
relations.hypotheses: F continuously differentiable on X; Y a real matrix; J(X) an interval enclosure of the Jacobian on X; c in X; all interval arithmetic outward-rounded.

relations.statement: If the finite union of boxes X_i contains the parameter domain D and F has no zero in any X_i, then F has no zero in D.
relations.hypotheses: D subset of union of X_i; finite family.

lemmas.statement: Conditional on a finite cover of D by boxes each satisfying the Krawczyk disjointness test, the 180-residual system has no zero in D.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem cover_excludes {n : Nat} (F : (Fin n -> Real) -> (Fin 180 -> Real)) (D : Set (Fin n -> Real)) (B : Finset (Set (Fin n -> Real))) (hcov : D ⊆ ⋃ X ∈ B, X) (hex : ∀ X ∈ B, ∀ x ∈ X, F x ≠ 0) : ∀ x ∈ D, F x ≠ 0 := by sorry

near_misses.claim: Exclusion of the regions in MUB6-C28 and MUB6-PAPER-CLOSE-COLUMNS establishes the global claim.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Those regions do not cover D; the cover must be complete.

near_misses.claim: A UNRESOLVED_BOX result from a chart counts as exclusion.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Exclusion requires K(X) disjoint from X; unresolved means the test failed.

near_misses.claim: Exclusion of zeros of the 618- or 666-equation systems follows from the 180-residual cover.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Containing boxes for those systems are unresolved; no cover is established.

open_obligations: No complete box cover exists; containing boxes of the 618- and 666-equation systems are unresolved.
No existing declarations in @SRC, so all references are proposed_new.
Formalization of the Krawczyk operator and its enclosure theorem is not done.
Relation between the 180-residual system and the 618/666-equation systems is not stated.
